card.summary: The Enhanced Cybersecurity for SNAP Act of 2026 directs federal agencies and states to improve the cybersecurity and digital security of Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) cards used in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program. It mandates a transition from magnetic stripe cards to secure chip-enabled EBT cards, sets rules for state-operated digital user interfaces, establishes federal reimbursements for card upgrades and a grant program for certain retailers, and prohibits certain password and PIN complexity requirements.

summary: The Enhanced Cybersecurity for SNAP Act of 2026 amends the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 to improve cybersecurity and digital services relating to Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) cards used under the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). The bill requires the Secretary of Agriculture to issue new regulations updating EBT card technology—specifically mandating the transition from magnetic stripe cards to chip-enabled cards—and sets rules regarding online transaction security, replacement cards, fees, retailer terminals, and reporting requirements.

affected_groups.effect: Will receive chip-enabled EBT cards, can request replacements within three business days without certain fees, and gain access to enhanced digital user interfaces, transaction notifications, and fraud reporting tools.

Must update user interfaces, issue chip-enabled cards, adhere to federal password and PIN standards, and follow new standards for replacing damaged or stolen cards, with reasonable costs reimbursed by the federal government.
Must ensure all retail locations use chip-enabled payment terminals to remain authorized or reauthorized to accept SNAP benefits.
affected_groups.group: Retail food stores and wholesale food concerns

key_provisions: Requires the Secretary of Agriculture to promulgate and regularly update cybersecurity and digital service regulations for EBT cards and mobile technologies to match private sector and federal security safeguards.
Mandates that States transition to issuing chip-enabled EBT cards without magnetic stripes over specific timelines, eventually phasing out magnetic stripe cards entirely.
Prohibits State agencies from charging replacement fees for EBT cards that malfunction, expire, are required to be replaced by new regulations, or are compromised by external fraud.
Requires States to provide replacement EBT cards within three business days of a request if a card is damaged, malfunctioning, stolen, or frozen due to fraud.
Requires retail and wholesale food stores participating in SNAP to have chip-enabled payment terminals at each location.
Establishes a grant program to help eligible entities in areas with limited grocery access to upgrade to chip-compatible payment terminals.
Directs the Department of Agriculture to publish periodic public reports on benefit theft trends, online transaction security, and EBT security in Puerto Rico.
missing_information: The total cost of implementation and reimbursements for States and retailers is not specified.
Specific funding amounts for the grant program to help retailers upgrade payment terminals are not stated.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Enhanced Cybersecurity for SNAP Act of 2026 amends the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 to improve cybersecurity and digital services relating to Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) cards used under the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). The bill requires the Secretary of Agriculture to issue new regulations updating EBT card technology—specifically mandating the transition from magnetic stripe cards to chip-enabled cards—and sets rules regarding online transaction security, replacement cards, fees, retailer terminals, and reporting requirements.
summary_detail.significance: This bill significantly updates the technological infrastructure of the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program by shifting millions of EBT users and participating retailers away from magnetic stripe cards toward secure chip-enabled technology. It impacts federal agencies, state administration, authorized food retailers, and low-income households reliant on SNAP by introducing strict timelines for cybersecurity upgrades, fraud prevention, and benefit replacement standards.
